first_impression.reaction: My assistant sent it because Greece is on the list for next summer. The first screen is about packages, which is not how we plan, but the tone is calm and it says where packages part ways, so she kept going. Her summary: almost everything here is for small weddings, but Amirandes takes 300, Four Seasons will work with our own people, and the places we would actually look at, Amanzoe, Costa Navarino, Santa Marina, get one line saying they write a proposal on request. I read the exclusive use and transfers parts myself.

journey.quote: Greece wedding packages usually bundle the ceremony, its set-up, a coordinator and some help with the paperwork.
journey.reaction: A bundle with some help with the paperwork. That is not a wedding for 300 people. I can see the page is not written for me, but it is honest about it.

journey.quote: Exclusive use, guest rooms, transfers and outside suppliers are where packages differ most, so ask about each in writing.
journey.reaction: Those are exactly my questions, and 'in writing' is the right instinct. Good.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone and quotes in AUD.
journey.reaction: Which time zone? We are in Dubai, Sydney and London. This is written for a different family.

journey.quote: In Athens, Four Seasons Astir Palace publishes a list of [wedding inclusions](https://www.fourseasons.com/athens/weddings/planning/) that reads like a hotel's promise rather than a ceremony bundle: the wedding night for the couple, a menu tasting for up to four, a dedicated in-house wedding specialist, a service team on the day, premium tables, chairs and linens, and fine silver and china.
journey.reaction: Finally a hotel that sounds like the level we expect. 'A hotel's promise rather than a ceremony bundle' is the right distinction.

journey.quote: Deluxe Dream brings welcome drinks and an event coordinator present throughout the stay, Ultimate Passion a tasting dinner from the wedding menu and a massage the day before, and Essential Elegance a private brunch for the couple and guests and a farewell dinner.
journey.reaction: Tier names like a spa menu. My assistant would skip this paragraph.

journey.quote: Angsana Corfu's 2026 brochure describes a Special Wedding Offer: a credit towards a future stay with the group and, above a stated minimum food and beverage spend, a complimentary night for the couple in a sea-view suite or villa with breakfast the next day.
journey.reaction: A credit and a free night for spending enough. This is discount talk, and it makes the whole page feel like it is selling deals.

journey.quote: Amirandes, Grecotel, near Heraklion, offers its VIP Beach or chapel and dedicated wedding specialists for up to 300 guests, without a published package.
journey.reaction: Three hundred guests. That is our number, and 'without a published package' is how it should be. My assistant flagged this one.

journey.quote: [Costa Navarino](https://www.costanavarino.com/weddings-greece/) in the Peloponnese, [Grecotel Corfu Imperial](https://www.grecotel.com/corfuimperial/weddings-corfu/), [Amanzoe](https://www.aman.com/resorts/amanzoe/celebrations), [Santa Marina](https://www.santa-marina.gr/weddings-celebrations/) on Mykonos and [Katikies](https://www.katikies.com/events/) in Santorini and Mykonos write a proposal on request rather than publishing package inclusions.
journey.reaction: These are the names we would actually consider, and they are all in one sentence at the bottom of a section. The article spends paragraphs on donkeys and massages and one line on my shortlist.

journey.quote: Is the space yours alone, and which space is it?
journey.reaction: The right question, asked plainly. Most planners would not make the distinction between a terrace and the property.

journey.quote: And if you want the whole hotel, Canaves Collection takes buyout requests per property, from Canaves Sunday with 10 rooms for 22 guests to Canaves Epitome with 53 rooms for up to 170, with no buyout inclusions published.
journey.reaction: Good that the whole-hotel question is raised at all. But 170 is the ceiling, so Santorini is out for us. Useful to know quickly.

journey.quote: Melenos suggests reserving the whole hotel for at least three nights, as a suggestion rather than a condition, with more guests in its village apartments a 10 minute walk away.
journey.reaction: Closing the hotel for three nights is the right idea. Putting guests in village apartments down the road is not something my family would do.

journey.quote: In peak season, traffic congestion is severe in the main cities and on the islands, and only licensed taxis with the meter running should be used.
journey.reaction: Licensed taxis with the meter running. Nothing about private cars, arrivals or helicopters. This is where I feel like a tourist, not a client.

journey.quote: Four Seasons will work with the florist of your choice, and its specialist works "with you or your consultant".
journey.reaction: We bring our own people. A hotel that expects that is the kind I want to talk to.

journey.quote: Euphoria's packages "are complete packages, and their items are not interchangeable", with no refund or alternative for a service you skip.
journey.reaction: Exactly my fear: a fixed set I cannot change. Fair to warn, but it confirms most of this page is not for us.

journey.quote: Melenos lists a rehearsal dinner, live music, a private boat excursion and donkeys to carry the couple to the ceremony as additional services.
journey.reaction: Donkeys. My assistant would laugh and move on.

journey.section: How to compare two quotes like for like
journey.quote: Ask each venue to answer the same ten points in writing.
journey.reaction: A sensible list, but none of the ten mentions security, privacy, press or closing the property to the public. Those are the first three questions we would ask.

journey.section: How to compare two quotes like for like
journey.quote: It is unfinished.
journey.reaction: Short and sure. I like that line.

journey.section: Venue package, planner or building your own
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is a single point of contact who plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world.
journey.reaction: One contact, anywhere in the world. That is closer to what we need than anything else on the page.

journey.section: For Australian couples: currency, deposits and insurance
journey.quote: A Greek package priced abroad is paid from Australia, often months apart, so the terms around the money matter as much as the inclusions.
journey.reaction: Not relevant to us. My assistant skipped the section.

journey.section: Compare your shortlist with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: One person start to finish is right. 'For Australian couples' at the very end tells me again who this is really for.

unanswered_questions: Can Amirandes, Four Seasons Astir Palace, Costa Navarino or Amanzoe be closed to the public for three days for 200 to 400 guests?
Can our own security team work alongside the venue's, and how are staff, vendors and guest photography handled for privacy and press?
Can private cars, meet-and-greet arrivals and private aviation or helicopter transfers be arranged instead of taxis?
Can a multi-day celebration with our own catering requirements and family customs be run at one of these venues?
Has Wedded Wonderland delivered a wedding of this size in Greece, and is there a private or referral channel to someone senior?

turn_offs_found.quote: Angsana Corfu's 2026 brochure describes a Special Wedding Offer: a credit towards a future stay with the group and, above a stated minimum food and beverage spend, a complimentary night for the couple in a sea-view suite or villa with breakfast the next day.
turn_offs_found.why: A 'Special Wedding Offer' with a credit and a complimentary night is loyalty-scheme language. Introduced with 'Then there are offers', it frames the reader as someone chasing a deal, which is how a standard package client is treated.

turn_offs_found.quote: Deluxe Dream brings welcome drinks and an event coordinator present throughout the stay, Ultimate Passion a tasting dinner from the wedding menu and a massage the day before, and Essential Elegance a private brunch for the couple and guests and a farewell dinner.
turn_offs_found.why: Named tiers listed one after another make Greece read as a menu to pick from. Accurate to the venue, but it takes up more space than the bespoke venues get in the whole article.

turn_offs_found.quote: In peak season, traffic congestion is severe in the main cities and on the islands, and only licensed taxis with the meter running should be used.
turn_offs_found.why: A tourist safety tip about taxi meters pitches the transfers section at an ordinary traveller and leaves private logistics unmentioned.

would_share_with: My assistant, to ask Amirandes and Four Seasons Astir Palace about full closure, rooms and working with our own security
My mother, for the line that Costa Navarino, Amanzoe and Santa Marina write proposals on request

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [compare your shortlist with a Wedded Advisor](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=greece-wedding-packages&utm_content=closing), or return to [our curated Greece wedding collection](https://weddedwonderland.com/destinations/europe/greece).
cta_reaction.why: The close is quiet, there are no prices and no 'value' talk, which I prefer. But we don't compare packages, and the page keeps saying AUD and Australian couples. I wouldn't fill in a web form. Through my assistant or a referral, possibly.

top_3_changes: Give the venues that write proposals on request (Costa Navarino, Amanzoe, Santa Marina, Katikies, and Amirandes and Four Seasons at scale) more than one sentence, framed as the bespoke route for large weddings, so a reader at that level sees her path through the article, using only what those venues publish.

Add privacy and scale to the ten comparison questions, for example whether the whole property can be closed, how the venue works with a private security team and what it allows for guest and vendor photography, so the checklist covers large and high-profile weddings too.

Tone down the deal and tourist signals: shorten or reposition the Angsana 'Special Wedding Offer' paragraph and its 'Then there are offers' lead-in, balance the licensed-taxi line with a question about private transfers, and drop 'for Australian couples' from the closing advisor line so families flying from elsewhere still feel addressed.
